newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine firms bullish on 1997 economy, investment.
newsitem.headline: Argentine firms bullish on 1997 economy, investment.

text.p: More than eight out of 10 leading Argentine companies expect economic activity to pick up next year and nearly seven out of 10 believe their own investments will rise, according to a poll published Monday.

The survey of 173 major companies in El Cronista newspaper showed 83.3 percent expect activity to be "somewhat better" in 1997, 7.0 percent forecast it will be "much better" and 8.5 percent see no change. Only 0.7 percent see it shrinking.

A vast majority of 85 percent expect better sales next year than in 1996 and 67.6 percent are preparing to increase investment. Only 4.2 percent see their investments falling in 1997 and 28.2 percent predict they will remain constant.
In terms of staffing levels, 55 percent have no plans to hire or fire significantly while 35.2 percent expect to take on new staff. Nearly one in 10 expect to reduce the payroll.
As for the political outlook, 57.7 percent expect mid-term Congressional elections next year to influence business levels "somewhat" and 12.7 percent see it having a big impact.

Roque Fernandez is seen remaining Economy Minister until the end of President Carlos Menem's second term in 1999 by 45.8 percent while 31.7 percent see him stepping down next year and 18.3 percent think he will leave in 1998.
